definitions.explanation: Actions taken after an event, incident, or main process to address remaining issues, clean up, or resolve consequences. Used in business, administrative, disaster management, and technical contexts.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}の{事後処理|じごしょり}に{追|お}われている。
examples.english: We are busy dealing with the aftermath of the accident.

examples.japanese: イベント{終了後|しゅうりょうご}の{事後処理|じごしょり}には{三日|みっか}ほどかかる{見込|みこ}みだ。
examples.english: Post-event follow-up is expected to take about three days.

examples.japanese: {事後処理|じごしょり}を{怠|おこた}ると{問題|もんだい}が{長引|ながび}くので、{迅速|じんそく}に{対応|たいおう}することが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: If you neglect the follow-up, problems will drag on, so it is important to respond quickly.

notes:
Composed of {事後|じご} (after the fact, post-) and {処理|しょり} (processing, handling). A versatile compound used whenever there are loose ends to tie up after a main event or process.

USAGE:
Common in business (wrapping up after a project), disaster response (cleanup and recovery), legal contexts (handling consequences), and IT (post-processing of data). The term emphasizes that work remains to be done even after the main activity is over.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事後処理|じごしょり}に{当|あ}たる: to handle the aftermath
- {事後処理|じごしょり}に{追|お}われる: to be chased by post-event tasks
- {事後処理|じごしょり}を{行|おこな}う: to carry out post-processing
- {事後処理|じごしょり}が{遅|おく}れる: post-processing is delayed

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {後始末|あとしまつ}: cleanup, tidying up after — more colloquial and often implies cleaning up someone's mess
- {後処理|あとしょり}: post-processing — similar meaning but slightly more casual; common in technical/IT contexts
- {事後対応|じごたいおう}: post-event response — focuses on responding to consequences rather than routine processing
- {善後策|ぜんごさく}: remedial measures — emphasizes finding the best solution after something has gone wrong
